questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, highlighters, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. There are forty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any working should be done in this booklet. An Olympic athlete of mass 80kg competes in a 100m race. What is the best estimate of his mean kinetic energy during the race?

options.A: 4 × 10 2 J B 4 × 10 3 J C 4 × 10 4 J D 4 × 10 5 J Space for working

The equation relating these quantities is    a2  L 3+ = QT 2 sinθ  P    Where a is the internal radius of the tube and P and Q are constants. Which line gives the correct units for P and Q? P Q

A tennis ball is released from rest at the top of a tall building. Which graph best represents the variation with time t of the acceleration a of the ball as it falls, assuming that the effect of air resistance is not negligible?

options.C: D a a 0 0 0 t 0 t Space for working

questions.questionText: A ball is released from rest on a smooth slope XY. It moves down the slope, along a smooth horizontal surface YZ and rebounds inelastically at Z. Then it moves back to Y and comes to rest momentarily somewhere on XY. X Y Z Which velocity-time graph represents the motion of the ball? velocity

options.C: 0 time velocity
options.D: 0 time Space for working

questions.questionText: A body falling in a uniform gravitational field encounters air resistance. The air resistance increases until terminal velocity is reached. Which factor does not affect its terminal velocity?

options.B: the height from which the body falls
options.C: the mass of the body
options.D: the shape of the body

questions.questionText: A boy throws a ball vertically upwards. It rises to a maximum height, where it is momentarily at rest, and then falls back to his hands. Which row gives the acceleration of the ball at various stages in its motion? (Take vertically upwards as positive. Ignore air resistance.) at maximum rising falling height –2 –2

options.D: +9.81ms 0 –9.81ms Space for working

questions.questionText: An ice-hockey puck slides along a horizontal, frictionless ice-rink surface. It collides inelastically with a wall at right angles to its path, and then rebounds along its original path. Which graph shows the variation with time t of the momentum p of the puck?

options.A: B C D p p p p 0 0 0 0 0 t 0 t 0 t 0 t

questions.questionText: What is the definition of the force on a body?

options.A: the mass of the body multiplied by its acceleration
options.B: the power input to the body divided by its velocity
options.C: the rate of change of momentum of the body
options.D: the work done on the body divided by its displacement Space for working

questions.questionText: A car accelerates from rest. The graph shows the momentum of the car plotted against time. momentum time What is the meaning of the gradient of the graph at a particular time?

options.A: the resultant force on the car
options.C: the kinetic energy of the car
options.D: the rate of change of kinetic energy of the car

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a child’s balancing game.

A ladder rests in equilibrium on rough ground against a rough wall. P rough G wall Q rough ground Its weight W acts through the centre of gravity G. Forces also act on the ladder at P and at Q. These forces are P and Q respectively. Which vector triangle represents the forces on the ladder?

options.A: B C D P P P P W W Q Q W Q W Q Space for working

questions.questionText: A ruler of length 0.30m is pivoted at its centre. Equal and opposite forces of magnitude 2.0N are applied to the ends of the ruler, creating a couple as shown. 2.0N 50° ruler pivot 50° 2.0N What is the magnitude of the torque of the couple on the ruler when it is in the position shown?
The first column in the table gives four examples of work being done. The second column gives more detail of the action. Which row is not correct? example detail

options.A: a girl dives from a diving work is done by the girl board into a swimming pool against gravity as she falls
options.B: a man pushes a car work is done by the along a level road man against friction
options.C: an electron is accelerated towards work is done on the electron a positively-charged plate by the electric field of the plate
options.D: a piston is pushed outwards work is done on the as a gas expands atmosphere by the gas Space for working

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a particle X, with kinetic energy E , about to collide with a stationary particle Y. k Both particles have the same mass. X Y After colliding, X and Y travel onwards together as a single larger particle. How much kinetic energy is lost in the collision? E E 3E

options.A: 0 B k C k D k

questions.questionText: An electric motor is required to produce 120W of mechanical output power. The efficiency of the motor is 80%. Which row is correct? electrical power waste heat output input to motor/W from motor/W

options.D: 150 120 Space for working

questions.questionText: A mass m is situated in space in a uniform gravitational field. gravitational P Q field lines x When the mass moves through a displacement x, from P to Q, it loses an amount of potential energy E. Which row correctly specifies the magnitude and the direction of the acceleration due to the gravity in this field? magnitude direction E

options.C: → x E
options.D: ← x Space for working

questions.questionText: A trolley runs from P to Q along a track. At Q its potential energy is 50kJ less than at P. trolley P Q At P, the kinetic energy of the trolley is 5kJ. Between P and Q, the work the trolley does against friction is 10kJ. What is the kinetic energy of the trolley at Q?

The Young modulus of steel is determined using a length of steel wire and is found to have the value E. Another experiment is carried out using a wire of the same steel, but of half the length and half the diameter. What value is obtained for the Young modulus in the second experiment?

options.A: 1 E B E C 2E D 4E Space for working

questions.questionText: A rubber band is stretched and then relaxed to its original length. The diagram shows the force-extension graph for this process. Q force P area X area Y R O e extension As the force is increased, the curve follows the path OPQ to extension e. As the force is reduced, the curve follows the path QRO to return to zero extension. The area labelled X is between the curves OPQ and QRO. The area labelled Y is bounded by the curve QRO and the horizontal axis. Which statement about the process is correct?

options.A: Area X is the energy which heats the band as it is stretched to e.
options.B: (Area X + area Y) is the minimum energy required to stretch the band to e.
options.C: Area X is the elastic potential energy stored in the band when it is stretched to e.
options.D: (Area Y – area X) is the net work done on the band during the process. Space for working

questions.questionText: Pollen grains are suspended in a liquid and are illuminated strongly. When observed under a microscope they are seen to be in continuous random motion. What is the reason for this?

options.C: molecules of the liquid colliding with the pollen grains
options.D: pollen grains colliding with each other

questions.questionText: Why does the pressure increase when a sealed container of gas is heated?

options.A: The gas molecules collide more often with each other.
options.B: The gas molecules expand when they are heated.
options.C: The gas molecules travel faster and hit the walls of the container more often.
options.D: There are more gas molecules present to collide with the walls of the container.

questions.questionText: A metal cube of side l is placed in a vice and compressed elastically by two opposing forces F. F l F l metal cube How will ∆l, the amount of compression, relate to l?
When describing the behaviour of a spring, the spring constant is used. Different loads are used to extend the spring by different amounts. To find the spring constant, which quantities are required?

options.A: the elastic limit and the loads
options.B: the elastic limit, extensions and the length of the spring
options.C: the loads and the extensions of the spring
options.D: the loads and the length of the spring

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a view from above of a double slit interference demonstration. L is a monochromatic light source with a vertical filament. B is a barrier with two narrow vertical slits and S is a screen upon which interference fringes form. L

options.B: S The intensity is I at a point on the screen where the centre of the fringe pattern forms. What is the intensity, at the same point, when one of the slits is covered up? I I I I

questions.questionText: P is a source emitting infra-red radiation and Q is a source emitting ultra-violet radiation. The figures in the table are suggested values for the wavelengths emitted by P and Q. Which row is correct? wavelength wavelength emitted by P/m emitted by Q/m

Coherent waves are produced at P and at Q and travel outwards in all directions. The line RS is halfway between P and Q and perpendicular to the line joining P and Q. The distance RS is much greater than the distance PQ. P R Q NOT TO SCALE X Y S Along which line, or lines, is an interference pattern observed?

options.C: XY only
options.D: neither RS nor XY Space for working

questions.questionText: Travelling waves of wavelength 20cm are created in the air columns in a closed pipe P and an open pipe Q. The lengths of the pipes are shown. P Q 35cm 50cm In which pipe or pipes are stationary waves formed?

options.C: Q only
options.D: neither P nor Q

questions.questionText: The diagram shows an insulating rod with equal and opposite point charges at each end. An electric field of strength E acts on the rod in a downwards direction. E +Q –Q Which row is correct? resultant force resultant torque

options.C: zero anti-clockwise
options.D: downwards anti-clockwise Space for working

questions.questionText: Two horizontal parallel plate conductors are separated by a distance of 5.0mm in air. The lower plate is earthed and the potential of the upper plate is +50V. What is the electric field strength E at a point midway between the plates?

options.C: 2.0 × 104Vm–1 downwards
options.D: 2.0 × 104Vm–1 upwards

questions.questionText: An atomic nucleus emits a β-particle. What change does this cause to the proton number and the nucleon number of the nucleus? proton number nucleon number

options.D: +1 0 Space for working

questions.questionText: Which statement is not valid?

options.A: Current is the speed of the charged particles that carry it.
options.B: Electromotive force (e.m.f.) is the energy converted to electrical energy from other forms, per unit charge.
options.C: The potential difference (p.d.) between two points is the work done in moving unit charge from one point to the other.
options.D: The resistance between two points is the p.d. between the two points, per unit current.

questions.questionText: Which statement about electrical resistivity is correct?

options.A: The resistivity of a material is numerically equal to the resistance in ohms of a cube of that material, the cube being of side length one metre and the resistance being measured between opposite faces.
options.B: The resistivity of a material is numerically equal to the resistance in ohms of a one metre length of wire of that material, the area of cross-section of the wire being one square millimetre and the resistance being measured between the ends of the wire.
options.C: The resistivity of a material is proportional to the cross-sectional area of the sample of the material used in the measurement.
options.D: The resistivity of a material is proportional to the length of the sample of the material used in the measurement. Space for working

questions.questionText: A cell, two resistors of equal resistance and an ammeter are used to construct four circuits. The resistors are the only parts of the circuits that have resistance. In which circuit will the ammeter show the greatest reading?

options.C: D

questions.questionText: Three resistors of resistance R, 2R and 3R are connected in parallel. R 2R 3R Using I to represent the current through the resistor of resistance R, which row represents the relationships between the currents through the resistors? resistor resistance R 2R 3R
A cell of e.m.f. E and internal resistance r is connected in series with a switch S and an external resistor of resistance R. E r P Q R S The p.d. between P and Q is V. When S is closed,

options.A: V decreases because there is a p.d. across R.
options.B: V decreases because there is a p.d. across r.
options.C: V remains the same because the decrease of p.d. across r is balanced by the increase of p.d. across R.
options.D: V remains the same because the sum of the p.d.s across r and R is still equal to E. Space for working

options.C: = t P
options.D: PQ = EI Space for working
